ai.literal: Without a game board, playing with a piece is like; without thorough learned books, holding an assembly.
ai.translation: To participate in an assembly of scholars without thorough learning is like playing a game of dice without a game board.
ai.modern: விளையாடும் பலகை இல்லாமல் வட்டு உருட்டி விளையாடுவதைப் போன்றது, முழுமையான நூலறிவு இல்லாமல் அறிஞர்கள் அவையில் பேசுவது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy to show the futility of unlearned people trying to engage in intellectual debates. The word 'vaṭṭu' refers to a playing piece or die, and 'araṅku' is the marked board required to play the game. Just as throwing dice without a board is meaningless and impossible to score, speaking in an assembly ('kōṭṭi') without comprehensive knowledge ('nirampiya nūl') is completely pointless. The poet emphasizes that thorough learning is the essential foundation for any intellectual discourse.

ai.literal: An unlearned man desiring speech is like she who lacks both breasts desiring womanhood.
ai.translation: An unlearned person's desire to speak in an assembly is like a woman lacking both breasts desiring to exhibit womanly charms.
ai.modern: கல்வி கற்காதவன் அவையில் பேச விரும்புவது, இரு மார்பகங்களும் இல்லாத ஒரு பெண் பெண்மையை விரும்பியதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a sharp, vivid analogy to illustrate the futility of an uneducated person attempting to speak in public. The word 'காமுறுதல்' means desiring or longing for something. Just as a woman who lacks breasts cannot successfully embody or express physical womanly beauty, an unlearned person cannot command respect or deliver a meaningful speech in an assembly. The comparison highlights that without the essential underlying quality, the desire to perform the associated role is entirely in vain.

parts.gloss: if they obtain / if they can

ai.literal: Even those who are unlearned are very excellent, if they can manage to remain without speaking before the learned.
ai.translation: Even those who are unlearned are highly excellent, if they can manage to remain silent in the presence of the learned.
ai.modern: கற்றவர்களின் முன்னிலையில் பேசாமல் அமைதியாக இருக்க முடிந்தால், கல்வி கற்காதவர்களும் மிகவும் நல்லவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the value of silence for those who lack education. It states that even unlearned individuals can be considered highly excellent if they possess the self-restraint to remain silent in the presence of scholars. By not speaking, they prevent their lack of knowledge from being exposed, thereby preserving their dignity. The phrase 'நனிநல்லர்' (highly excellent) shows how silence can elevate their worth, while 'சொல்லாதிருக்கப் பெறின்' (if they can manage to remain silent) emphasizes the self-control required to do so.

ai.literal: An unlearned man's natural intelligence, exceedingly good although it be, will not accept those who possess wisdom.
ai.translation: Even if the natural intelligence of an unlearned person is exceedingly great, those who possess true wisdom will not value it.
ai.modern: கல்லாதவனுடைய அறிவு மிகச் சிறந்ததாக இருந்தாலும், அறிவுடையவர்கள் அதனை ஏற்றுக்கொள்ள மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that natural brightness or sharp-wittedness in an unlearned person is not highly valued by the wise. The word 'ஒட்பம்' refers to natural mental sharpness or brilliance. Even if this brilliance appears 'கழிய நன்று' (exceedingly good), those who possess true wisdom ('அறிவுடையார்') will not accept or respect it ('கொள்ளார்'). This is because natural wit, without the discipline and depth of systematic learning, is unstable and lacks real substance.

ai.literal: The pretended worth of an unlearned person, when meeting others and speaking, ruin will occur to it.
ai.translation: The apparent dignity of an unlearned person will instantly collapse the moment they meet others and begin to speak.
ai.modern: கல்லாத ஒருவனுடைய தகைமையானது (மதிப்பு), அவன் பிறரைச் சந்தித்துப் பேசத் தொடங்கும்போது கெட்டுப் போய்விடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how silence can mask ignorance, but only temporarily. An unlearned person might carry themselves with an air of dignity and worth ('தகைமை') that deceives others at first glance. However, the moment they come face-to-face ('தலைப்பெய்து') with others and engage in intellectual discourse ('சொல்லாட'), their lack of knowledge is exposed. Their superficial reputation immediately suffers a ruinous collapse ('சோர்வு படும்') because speech inevitably reveals the depth of one's mind.

words.gloss: those who are of the mere measure

ai.literal: Except for the mere measure of being called those who exist, unlearned people are like barren land that yields nothing.
ai.translation: Except for the mere fact that they are said to exist, those who are unlearned are like barren, useless land.
ai.modern: உயிரோடு இருக்கிறார்கள் என்று சொல்லும் அளவினரே அல்லாமல், கல்லாதவர்கள் ஒன்றும் விளையாத களர் நிலத்திற்கு ஒப்பாவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares unlearned people to barren, saline soil (களர்) which cannot produce any useful crops. The author states that the uneducated are like this useless land, serving no productive purpose for society. The phrase 'உளரென்னும் மாத்திரையர்' emphasizes that their only attribute is that they are physically alive, and nothing more. They lack the intellectual and moral fruitfulness that comes with learning.

ai.literal: The beauty and charm of one who does not have subtle, excellent, penetrating intellect is like a well-made, adorned clay doll.
ai.translation: The physical beauty and charm of a person who lacks a subtle, deep, and penetrating intellect is like a beautifully adorned doll made of clay.
ai.modern: நுட்பமான, சிறந்த, ஊடுருவி அறியும் அறிவு இல்லாதவனுடைய அழகும் கவர்ச்சியும், மண்ணால் செய்யப்பட்டு அழகாக அலங்கரிக்கப்பட்ட பொம்மையைப் போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares an unlearned person who lacks deep, penetrating intellect to a beautifully crafted clay doll. Although the clay doll is painted and decorated to look attractive, it lacks life, movement, and real utility. Similarly, a person may possess great physical beauty and charm, but without the inner light of subtle, sharp knowledge, that beauty is superficial and useless. The poet uses the contrast between the external beauty of the doll and its lifeless clay substance to emphasize that true human worth comes from learning and intellect, not physical appearance.

words.gloss: with the good or learned people

ai.literal: Than the poverty befallen with the learned, the wealth accumulated with the unlearned is indeed more painful.
ai.translation: More painful than the poverty that afflicts the learned is the wealth that accumulates with the unlearned.
ai.modern: அறிவுடைய நல்லவர்களிடம் உள்ள வறுமையை விட, கல்லாதவர்களிடம் சேர்ந்துள்ள செல்வம் மிகவும் துன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares two undesirable states: poverty among the wise and wealth among the ignorant. The poet asserts that while the poverty of learned people is sad, the wealth possessed by uneducated, ignorant people is even more painful and harmful to society. The word 'நல்லார்' refers to good, learned people, while 'கல்லார்' refers to those who lack education. The term 'திரு' represents wealth or fortune, which becomes a source of distress when held by those without wisdom.

ai.literal: Even if born in high status, those who have not learned, even though born in low status, those who have learned, that much they do not have greatness.
ai.translation: Even if born of high birth, those who are unlearned lack the dignity and greatness of those who, though of low birth, are learned.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த குலத்தில் பிறந்திருந்தாலும் கல்வி கற்காதவர்கள், தாழ்ந்த குலத்தில் பிறந்திருந்தாலும் கல்வி கற்றவர்களின் அளவிற்குப் பெருமை இல்லாதவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that true dignity and greatness come from learning, not from the status of one's birth. The author contrasts those born into high status who remain unlearned with those born into low status who acquire knowledge. The word 'pāṭu' is used here in the sense of greatness or worthiness. The verse asserts that the unlearned, regardless of their high birth, can never match the intrinsic worth and respect commanded by the learned, even if the latter are of humble origins.

words.gloss: compared to those who have learned

ai.literal: Compared to beasts, human beings are like; compared to those who have learned shining books, the other people.
ai.translation: As beasts are to human beings, so are the unlearned when compared to those who have studied illustrious books.
ai.modern: விளக்கமான நூல்களைக் கற்றவர்களோடு ஒப்பிடும்போது, கல்லாதவர்கள் மனிதர்களோடு ஒப்பிடும்போது விலங்குகளைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a stark analogy to emphasize the value of education. It states that the difference between an unlearned person and an educated person is as vast as the difference between a beast and a human being. The word 'இலங்கு' (shining or illustrious) describes 'நூல்' (books of wisdom), suggesting that true learning brings light and clarity to the mind. Without this learning, a person remains at a level of existence comparable to animals, lacking the refined understanding that defines humanity.
